meta.subtitle: Revenue grew 34% with net cash and positive free cash flow, but GAAP losses and founder control temper the case

analystCommentary:
Viant is growing quickly. Second-quarter 2026 revenue rose 34%, and the MD&A describes strengthening advertiser demand across industry verticals, continued demand for connected TV and expanded use of its ViantAI product suite.

At $12.24 on October 2, 2026 the shares sit in the upper half of their 52-week range of $8.11 – $14.80. All 11 covering analysts rate Buy.

The growth is not yet showing up in GAAP profit: the company reported a net loss in the quarter, and gross profit is growing more slowly than revenue (see Financials). We think the balance sheet and cash generation give it room to invest through that, and that the price leaves upside if growth holds. Control by the founding family is the main governance caveat (see Management).

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Viant Technology Inc. is an advertising technology company. Its cloud-based demand side platform lets marketers and their agencies plan, buy and measure programmatic advertising across connected TV (CTV), streaming audio, digital out-of-home, mobile and desktop.

Viant earns platform fees, charged primarily as a percentage of spend or as a fixed price per thousand impressions, plus fees for its proprietary data, measurement and technology services. Its products include the ViantAI suite, Household ID and IRIS_ID. On May 1, 2026 it completed the acquisition of TVision, adding attention measurement and data capabilities.

The company was founded in 1999 and is headquartered in Irvine, California.

thesis.body: Viant is growing revenue at a rate well above FY25's, has no debt, and generates free cash flow. If it sustains growth near consensus and converts more of it into operating profit, the shares should move toward the Street's targets. The scenario math in Valuation supports a BUY, with a target below the Street's to reflect GAAP losses and the risks of a controlled company.

catalysts: Continued revenue growth in the seasonally strong fourth quarter.
Integration of TVision into Viant's measurement offering.
Adoption of AI Decisioning and the Outcomes performance solution.
A return to GAAP operating profit.
risks: Dependence on a select number of advertising agency holding companies.
Gross profit growing more slowly than revenue.
Data privacy rules and the loss of tracking signals.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue was $344.2M, up 19.0%, after growth of 29.7% in FY24. Operating margin turned positive at 1.2% in FY24 and reached 3.5% in FY25, and diluted EPS rose to $0.36 from $0.14.

Growth picked up in 2026. Second-quarter revenue was $104.3 million, up 34%, and first-half revenue rose 30%. The MD&A credits growing customer adoption of newer products and platform features.

The counter-case is profitability. Gross profit rose 27% to $45.5 million and contribution ex-TAC rose 24%, both slower than revenue, and the trailing gross margin has slipped to 44.5% from 45.8% in FY25. The company reported a net loss of $(1.8) million in the quarter against net income of $1.8 million a year earlier, and an operating margin of -3.7%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 26% to $14.2 million, so the gap between adjusted and GAAP results is wide.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Viant reports no debt, and trailing net debt to EBITDA is -6.4x, meaning cash well exceeds borrowings. The trailing current ratio is 2.34, down from 4.24 in FY21 but still comfortable.

That balance sheet lets the company keep investing in growth and fund acquisitions such as TVision without borrowing, which lowers the risk of the GAAP losses.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow was $51.7M in FY25, a 15.0% FCF margin, and FCF margins have been positive in four of the last five years. Capital expenditure is very small. The trailing FCF yield is 8.1%.

Cash generation is stronger than GAAP earnings because the business is light on capital and the losses include non-cash charges. That cash flow gives some valuation support even while GAAP profit is thin.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $12.24 DSP trades at 35.0x trailing earnings, 20.3x NTM earnings, ~15.6x FY27E earnings, 2.1x trailing sales and 20.7x trailing EV/EBITDA.

Consensus expects EPS of $0.60 for FY26E and $0.79 for FY27E, against FY25 diluted EPS of $0.36. The consensus basis is not stated; the company reports non-GAAP net income and Adjusted EBITDA, and with GAAP results negative in 2026 so far, the estimates are most likely on an adjusted basis.

The Street is uniformly positive: 11 Buy ratings, with a consensus target of $19.50, a median of $19.00 and a range of $17.00–$24.00.

We have no peer multiples to compare against.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Revenue keeps growing near the 2026 pace, TVision and ViantAI lift margins, and GAAP profit returns. The shares reach the Street median target.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Viant delivers close to consensus revenue, with margins improving slowly. The shares settle near the top of the 52-week range, still below the lowest Street target of $17.00.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: An agency holding company cuts spending or ad budgets tighten, revenue growth slows and losses persist. The shares fall back toward the 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because it requires only that Viant meets consensus revenue without a step-up in margins. Bull carries more weight than Bear because revenue growth has accelerated and the net cash position cushions a downturn. Bear still carries a quarter of the weight because revenue depends on a small number of agency holding companies and advertising budgets are cyclical.

The result is a weighted fair value of $14.35, an expected upside of +17.2% and a bear-case downside of -30.6%. That clears our BUY threshold.

Our $13–$16 target range brackets Base. It sits below the Street's range because we give more weight to the GAAP losses and governance risk than the Street does.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Viant reports a single segment. Revenue comes from platform fees under master service agreements and insertion orders, plus separate service fees for data management, media execution and advanced reporting. The MD&A says CTV represents a growing portion of activity on the platform.

moatFactors.name: Proprietary data and identity
moatFactors.body: Household ID, IRIS_ID and attention signals, now extended by TVision, give Viant data that customers can use to target and measure campaigns. The 10-Q warns that the effectiveness of the platform would decrease if its access to data were diminished.

moatFactors.name: Switching costs
moatFactors.body: The 10-Q says customers typically have relationships with numerous providers and can use both Viant's platform and competitors' without significant cost or disruption, and that contracts generally carry no long-term or exclusive obligations.

moatFactors.name: Independence
moatFactors.body: The MD&A says engagement with enterprise brands reflects advertiser interest in independent and transparent buy-side alternatives. In our view, that positioning helps win business but is not a barrier competitors cannot also offer.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NONE. Viant's data assets are useful, but its own filing says customers can switch between platforms easily and are not bound by long-term contracts. Its position depends on continued product improvement rather than structural protection, which is why we keep our target below the Street's despite the growth.

points: Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$442.6M, up 29%, and FY27E revenue of $533M. Given first-half growth of 30%, the FY26E figure looks achievable if fourth-quarter seasonality holds.
The MD&A expects continued benefit from the shift of advertising budgets from linear television to CTV. In our view, that shift is the main driver of the growth outlook.
AI Decisioning and Outcomes extend ViantAI toward automated campaign planning and execution. Their contribution is not yet quantified in the filing.
Management plans to keep increasing operating expenses to invest in growth, which may delay a return to GAAP profit.

management.leadership: Per the proxy statement dated April 2026, Tim Vanderhook is Chief Executive Officer and Chairman, and Chris Vanderhook is Chief Operating Officer and a director. They founded the company with their brother Russ Vanderhook, Senior Vice President and Co-Founder. Their long tenure gives continuity, and the recent acceleration in revenue growth reflects well on execution.
management.capitalAllocation: Viant pays no dividend and our data shows no repurchase amounts for FY21 to FY25. Its main capital decision in 2026 was the TVision acquisition, which expands into audience measurement. The 10-Q warns that TVision brings risks including the integration of panel-based measurement, the accuracy of measurement data and increased competition from established measurement providers. In our view, funding growth from internal cash rather than debt is the right approach for a business with this revenue volatility.
management.governance:
Viant is a controlled company. Per the proxy statement dated April 2026, Tim Vanderhook, Chris Vanderhook and Capital V LLC hold more than 50% of the voting power for the election of directors through Class B common stock, and the company uses exemptions from Nasdaq rules requiring a majority-independent board and fully independent compensation and nominating committees. The Board has determined that Max Valdes, Brett Wilson and Vivian Yang are independent.

The proxy also discloses an aircraft lease with Capital V, which the three brothers each own a one-third interest in, at $14,500 per flight hour during its initial term, renewing annually. For public holders, that combination of control and related-party dealings means fewer formal protections than at a widely held company.
management.insiderOwnership:
As of April 9, 2026, Capital V LLC held 42.86% of total voting power, Tim Vanderhook 13.63% and Chris Vanderhook 13.77%, with overlapping holdings among them. All executive officers and directors as a group held 29.43% of total voting power. Punch & Associates Investment Management, Inc. held 6.32% and BlackRock, Inc. 5.65% of the Class A common stock.

The founding family's economic stake aligns it with shareholders, but it also means outside holders have little influence over strategy or governance.

idiosyncratic: Customer concentration: the 10-Q says Viant receives a significant amount of revenue from a select number of advertising agency holding companies, and that losing advertising agencies as customers could harm the business.

Data and privacy: the 10-Q warns that changing legal obligations on data privacy and AI, and the restriction of third-party cookies and use of automated opt-out signals, could reduce the availability of data and the effectiveness of the platform.
Inventory access: the 10-Q says revenue could decline if access to advertising inventory diminishes or fails to grow.
Integration: TVision adds measurement-specific risks, set out in Management.
risks.systemic: The MD&A says advertising spend is closely tied to advertisers' financial performance, and that a downturn could hurt the digital advertising market and Viant's results. Revenue is also seasonal, with the fourth quarter historically the strongest, and political advertising can swing results across election cycles.

body: BUY, target range $13–$16, based on the scenarios in Valuation.
We would add conviction if gross margin stabilizes and GAAP operating profit returns. We would cut to HOLD if revenue growth slows sharply or if an agency holding company reduces its spending.
